methodology: Compiled from Wikipedia equipment lists (List of equipment of the Russian Ground Forces) and current open-source defense reporting (news outlets, manufacturer/state statements, export contract disclosures). Cross-referenced against Oryx ('Attack On Europe: Documenting Russian Equipment Losses'), the leading open-source visual-confirmation tracker for this war, to prioritize models with substantial documented combat use rather than obscure or single-instance variants. Unit costs for Russian systems are rarely officially confirmed and vary significantly across sources -- treat unit_cost_usd as rough open-source estimates, not verified procurement figures. Entries whose cost_confidence is 'low' rely on general open-source consensus rather than a specific citable transaction. In-service quantities and combat losses change continuously amid the ongoing war and are intentionally not included here (see Oryx for real-time loss counts).
notes_on_comparison_group: Use 'comparison_group' to match equivalent entries against ukrainian_military_equipment.json. Not every entry has a direct counterpart (e.g. Russia's Geran-2 pairs with Ukraine's Fire Point FP-1 as 'long_range_strike_drone'; Ukraine's Magura V5 has no close Russian equivalent).

equipment.name: T-90M Proryv

unit_cost_usd.basis: Russian state media / industry estimate, ~350 million rubles; not independently verified

equipment.combat_notes: Russia's most modern tank in wide service; flagship of modernized tank regiments since the 2022 invasion.

equipment.name: T-80BVM

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate; refurbishment of existing T-80BV hulls rather than new-build

specifications.main_armament: 125mm 2A46M5 smoothbore gun, 9M119 Refleks gun-launched ATGM capability

equipment.combat_notes: Russia's only gas-turbine-powered MBT in frontline service; deep modernization of stored T-80BV hulls, prized for cold-weather starting and mobility.

equipment.name: T-72B3

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for modernized refurbishment

equipment.combat_notes: Russia's single most numerous tank type in this war by a wide margin (Oryx-confirmed losses across multiple sub-variants, incl. the 'Obr. 2022' field upgrade, run into the hundreds).

equipment.name: BMP-3

unit_cost_usd.basis: Open-source estimate based on prior export contracts

equipment.combat_notes: Extensively used and lost by Russian forces in Ukraine; captured units also fielded by Ukrainian forces.

equipment.name: BMP-2

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for a legacy design

equipment.combat_notes: Older, more numerous predecessor to the BMP-3; still the most common IFV type on both sides of the war due to shared Soviet-era stockpiles.

equipment.name: BTR-82A
equipment.combat_notes: Russia's standard modern wheeled APC, an upgrade of the Soviet-era BTR-80 with a new turret and fire control system.

equipment.name: 2S19 Msta-S
equipment.combat_notes: Frequently cued by Orlan-10 UAVs for target correction.

equipment.name: 2S3 Akatsiya
equipment.combat_notes: Cold War-era system pulled from long-term storage in large numbers to make up for combat losses.

equipment.name: 2S1 Gvozdika

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for reactivated Soviet stock

equipment.combat_notes: One of the most widely produced SPHs in history (10,000+ built); used by both Russia and Ukraine from shared Soviet stockpiles.

equipment.name: 9A52-4 Tornado-S
equipment.combat_notes: Modernized, automated successor to the BM-30 Smerch heavy MLRS; direct counterpart to HIMARS.

equipment.name: BM-21 Grad

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for the launcher vehicle

equipment.combat_notes: The most numerous and widely proliferated MLRS in the world; still a mainstay unguided-rocket system for both sides.

equipment.name: TOS-1A Solntsepyok

unit_cost_usd.basis: Figure includes servicing, training, and ammunition (Ukrainian defense reporting)

equipment.combat_notes: Heavy 'flamethrower' rocket system for fortified positions; large size makes it a prime target, with roughly 31 confirmed lost by mid-decade.

equipment.name: 2K22 Tunguska
equipment.combat_notes: Combined gun-missile short-range air defense on a tracked chassis, providing mobile cover for armored columns.

equipment.name: Pantsir-S1
equipment.manufacturer: KBP Instrument Design Bureau / Ulyanovsk Mechanical Plant
equipment.combat_notes: Point-defense gun-missile system protecting high-value sites, reportedly including sites around Moscow and St. Petersburg.

equipment.name: Buk-M3
equipment.combat_notes: Modernized version of the Buk family (the same lineage implicated in the 2014 MH17 shootdown); used to defend against Ukrainian aircraft and missiles.

equipment.name: Krasukha-4

specifications.targets: Airborne radar, satellites, reconnaissance aircraft, drones

equipment.combat_notes: Mobile jamming system intended to blind enemy radar and disrupt drone/satellite links; a high-value target for Ukrainian strikes.

equipment.name: Orlan-10

unit_cost_usd.basis: Open-source estimates; a full system (2 aircraft + ground control station) reported near $150,000

equipment.combat_notes: Typically flown in teams of 2-3 (reconnaissance / electronic warfare / relay); central to Russian reconnaissance-strike targeting loops.

equipment.name: ZALA Lancet-3
equipment.combat_notes: Primary threat to Ukrainian artillery, armor, and air-defense vehicles in counter-battery engagements.

equipment.name: Geran-2 (Shahed-136)
equipment.manufacturer: Alabuga Special Economic Zone, Russia (licensed from Iran's Shahed Aviation Industries)

unit_cost_usd.basis: CSIS/RUSI open-source range for Russian domestic production

equipment.combat_notes: Volume weapon of Russia's long-range strike campaign against Ukrainian cities and infrastructure; launched in mass swarms alongside decoys (Gerbera) and the newer jet-powered Geran-4.

equipment.name: Su-35S Flanker-E

specifications.engines: 2x Saturn AL-41F1S turbofan with thrust vectoring

equipment.combat_notes: Russia's primary air-superiority fighter over the front; several lost to Ukrainian F-16s and Patriot batteries in 2026.

equipment.name: Su-34 Fullback

unit_cost_usd.basis: Widely varying open-source estimates ($36M-$85M reported); mid-range used here

specifications.armament: 30mm GSh-30-1 cannon + guided bombs, air-to-surface and anti-ship missiles

equipment.combat_notes: Russia's primary glide-bomb (UMPK/KAB) delivery platform, responsible for much of the war's aerial bombardment of Ukrainian front-line towns; over 35 confirmed losses.

equipment.name: Su-25 Grach

specifications.armament: 30mm twin-barrel cannon + rockets, bombs, guided munitions

equipment.combat_notes: Heavily armored Soviet-era close air support jet ('Frogfoot'); flown by both Russia and Ukraine from shared Cold War stocks.

equipment.name: Ka-52 Alligator
equipment.combat_notes: One of Russia's most heavily used ground-attack platforms; dozens confirmed lost to MANPADS and drones.

equipment.name: Mi-8 / Mi-17

unit_cost_usd.basis: General open-source estimate for modernized variants

specifications.roles: Troop transport, medevac, gunship variants (Mi-8AMTSh) with rocket pods and cannon

equipment.combat_notes: Backbone utility helicopter of Russian army aviation, produced in more variants and greater numbers than any other Soviet helicopter design.

equipment.name: 9M133 Kornet
equipment.combat_notes: Widely exported; used against Ukrainian armor throughout the war.

equipment.name: Admiral Grigorovich-class frigate

specifications.armament: 8x Kalibr/Oniks cruise missile VLS cells, Shtil-1 SAM, 100mm A-190 gun

equipment.combat_notes: Black Sea Fleet's primary land-attack strike asset, used repeatedly to launch Kalibr cruise missiles at Ukraine.

equipment.name: Kilo-class submarine (Improved, Project 636.3)
equipment.combat_notes: Black Sea Fleet submarine used to launch Kalibr cruise missile strikes on Ukraine from underwater, forcing Ukraine to develop long-range strike responses against Russian naval infrastructure.

equipment.name: Buyan-M / Karakurt-class corvette

specifications.armament: 8x Kalibr cruise missile VLS cells, 100mm gun

equipment.combat_notes: Small, shallow-draft missile corvette that lets Russia fire Kalibr cruise missiles from rivers and coastal waters, complicating Ukrainian targeting.
